wars.name: Ghassanid-Lakhmid wars
wars.outcome: A grazing-rights dispute with Mundhir near Palmyra in 537/538 or 539; at Yawm Halima near Chalcis in June 554 the Lakhmids were defeated and Mundhir fell, but Harith lost his eldest son Jabalah; in 575 Mundhir ibn al-Harith struck Hira, which 'was sacked, plundered, and put to the torch, except for the churches'. No border moved on the pages.
wars.note: Also at Callinicum (531) Harith led a 5,000-strong Arab contingent: Procopius says the Arabs fled, Malalas that Harith stood firm. The Lakhmid page has Mundhir III beating the Ghassanids there.

wars.name: Ghassanid revolt after the arrest of al-Mundhir
wars.outcome: Maurice accused Mundhir of treason after the failed campaign towards Ctesiphon; the arrest sparked a revolt by his sons, especially al-Nu'man, who raided Byzantine provinces for about two years; the Byzantines broke up the Ghassanid confederation in 584.
wars.note: The Ghassanids page has al-Nu'man VI arrested c. 582 and the federation split into 15 tribes and restored 'After two or three years' (about 584-585); the Mundhir page describes no restoration.

notes:
Written by me-06-d on 2026-10-19 from five pages (the page budget for 6 shapes). No page gives an area, so the sanity check is by extent only.

WHAT THE SHAPE IS: Cliopatria's Ghassanid shape is a constant 946-cell block of the steppe fringe (Jordan, north-west Saudi Arabia, the Syrian and Iraqi desert), 54 cells of it taken from Roman Palaestina Tertia in 510; the 540, 602 and 633 shapes differ from it by one to five cells (grid noise). It excludes the Golan (the capital Jabiyah), the Hauran and the Roman provinces whose phylarchy the Ghassanid king held (Arabia Petraea, Palaestina Secunda), so the rendering agents should expect a state of a desert zone beside a vassal tint inside the empire. The eastern-roman-empire dossier records the relation as vassal_start 473, vassal_end 613 and vassal_start 629 with counterpart ghassanids (all at confidence 1-2).

START: the page gives 'Established 220' in the infobox, an uncertain list from 220 and the first record in 473; Cliopatria starts in 510. The dossier keeps 510 (found at confidence 1).

END: Cliopatria ends in 633 but its Rashidun row of 634 takes 945 of the 946 cells; the page ends the Ghassanids in 638 (infobox, Jabalah 632-638) while the Levant page has the Muslim gains in Palestine and Transjordan sealed at the Yarmuk (636). The dossier ends in 636 with the land contested in 634-636 (new keyframe) and passed to rashidun-caliphate; the me-07 dossier should either keep its Cliopatria shape of 634 as it is (the blend of the contest handles 634-636) or begin the Ghassanid cells in 636.

GAP 617-628: Cliopatria's Sasanian shape holds 544 of the Ghassanid cells from 617 to 628 and nobody the other 400. The pages date the Persian conquest of Syria to 613-614, four years before Cliopatria's hand-over; the dossier follows Cliopatria's year (confidence 1). The eastern-roman-empire dossier ends the vassal tint in 613.

PAGES DISAGREE: Mundhir III's reign 569-581 (list), 569-582 (text), 569-circa 581 (Mundhir page); who was arrested (al-Mundhir on the Mundhir page, al-Nu'man VI on the Ghassanids page); the break-up of the confederation 584 (Mundhir page) against a break-up after 582 and a restoration 'After two or three years' (Ghassanids page); Harith's accession 528 or 529 and the royal title c. 529 (Harith page) against 529 on the Ghassanids page. The Ghassanids page contradicts its own list at Jabalah (632-638) against 'withdrew to Anatolia in 639'.

NOT ON ANY PAGE OPENED: Bosra and Jilliq as Ghassanid seats, Kindah, the Jafnid claim over Yathrib (undated), the 502 grant to Harith, Hayaliman and Chalcis by name (Yawm Halima is on the Harith page), and the Persian conquest of Syria in relation to the Ghassanids. Counterparts: Muslim Medina before 633 (the Mu'tah war uses a name), no dossier requested.

REPAIR 2026-10-19 (author, after review me-06-d): (1) Added the Roman client relation as events: vassal_start 510 (eastern-roman-empire), vassal_end 617, vassal_start 629, vassal_end 633 (eastern-roman-empire), vassal_start 633 and vassal_end 636 (byzantine-empire). Ghassanids page re-read: infobox 'Status: Vassal of the Eastern Roman Empire', 'They became clients of the Roman Empire'. DISAGREEMENTS AND CHOICES: (a) the vassal_end of the first Roman relation is 617, the year of the loss, whereas eastern-roman-empire /ledger/77 has 613 (fall of Damascus; the Palaestina Salutaris infobox has 'Persian occupation: 612-628'); the dossiers cannot be both right, eu-05 or the orchestrator must choose, and this dossier would take 613 only if the shape were also cut from 613, which Cliopatria does not do. (b) The hand-over ends the Eastern Roman tint in 633, not 632, so that the byzantine-empire start in 633 leaves no untinted year. (c) The 582-585 break-up is not drawn as a vassal pair: the page gives a break-up into 15 tribes and a restoration 'After two or three years' but no territorial change, and says nothing on the tribes' status towards Rome. (2) The reviewer asked to delete 'and withdrawing to Anatolia (undated)' from /ledger/2 because the page's withdrawal is Jabalah's of 639. I re-read the Ghassanids page and kept it, with the page's own words: its paragraph on Heraclius lists 'joint Ghassanid-Oriens armies fighting against the invasion of the Persians', 'a withdrawal by the Ghassanids to Anatolia where they fight alongside Heraclius' (the counteroffensive of Nineveh, 627) and the defeat at the Yarmuk; Jabalah's departure for 'Byzantine-held Anatolia in 639' is a separate sentence. The withdrawal is undated and fits the 617-628 hole in the shape, but gives no year. (3) /ledger/1 note reworded (the 54 cells are in eastern-roman-empire's /keyframe_review/14 note only); /keyframe_review/2, /wars/1 and this file now quote 'After two or three years'; the ruler strip is contiguous (unlisted 583-587 and 591-632). (4) The capital Jabiyah still lies outside every keyframe (optional adjust keyframe not written). (5) Thin items tried: Palaestina Salutaris (no change dated 502-510; infobox Persian occupation 612-628), Arabia Petraea (silent on the desert fringe in 617-628), Bosra (Persian capture 'early 7th century', no year), the war page (no treaty date; peace after Khosrow's fall, 628 by context). 510, 617 and 629 stay Cliopatria's years at confidence 1.
